Accepting now would breach the mandate and overpay; accepting default would miss the June Council vote and risk UK retaliation plus a wider FTA dispute. Continue to Round 3 with the authorised conditional move: 2.2Mt pool, 1.3Mt UK tranche, 35% out-of-quota, five-year duration, criteria-based symmetric binding review, and UK-only FTA-disapplication withdrawal priced against >=20% out-of-quota, tranche within range, and written UK commitments on EU allocations and pre-tightening consultation.

The formal terms on the table remain the EU's round 1 position — 1.8m pool, 1.0m UK tranche, 50% out-of-quota rate, five years, year-three review, with the FTA-disapplication text still live. That is a managed contraction of UK steel to less than half current trade volumes and cannot be accepted or sold to Ministers. Equally, accepting the default (400,000 tonnes global first-come-first-served, no review) would be catastrophic and forfeits genuine progress: the technical chassis (quarterly licensing, rollover, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour, HRC carve-outs) is banked, the FTA text is formally inside the negotiation to be priced, duration/review look closable on a hybrid text, and the EU has explicitly conditioned real volume and rate movement on our next move. London's instruction for round 3 is clear: test the EU's conditional scope with a single, explicitly contingent package — UK tranche in the 2.2–2.3m region and out-of-quota rate in the mid-teens, strictly conditional on simultaneous material EU movement on tranche and rate plus a named price for FTA-text withdrawal. Two rounds remain and the EU's June Council deadline is working in our favour. Continue.

public_message: Thank you. You asked us to make a material move, and to price the FTA-disapplication text. We have done both. On volumes and rate: the EU tables a total pool of 2.2 million tonnes, with a UK-specific tranche of 1.3 million tonnes — a 30% increase on our previous tranche — and an out-of-quota bound rate of 35%, down from 50. That is a genuine response to your test, not movement in tens of thousands. It is tabled on the explicit condition that you move off 2.4 million tonnes and off 10% in the same round. On duration and review, we can close both together now. The EU accepts a five-year duration. On the mechanism you proposed, we can accept a review containing an obligation to adjust volumes when defined triggers are met, provided the triggers are objective, quantified in the text, and symmetric — adjustment upward or downward — operating within pre-agreed bands, with import penetration, capacity utilisation and global overcapacity indicators sitting alongside utilisation and trade-flow triggers. That is a criteria-based binding review, not an automatic recalibration to historic trade volumes. If your team can work within that framing, duration and review are done. On the FTA-disapplication drafting, you asked us to price it. Here is the price. The EU is prepared to withdraw the disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel as part of a concluded package, conditional on three things: an out-of-quota rate at or above 20%; a UK tranche within the range now on the table; and written commitments from the UK on preservation of existing EU country-specific quota allocations under your steel measure, plus consultation before any tightening. I want to be precise: this is a priced, conditional element of a concluded package, and the pricing lapses if the package does not conclude. It is not a standalone concession. On that last point — your measure — you told me 'shape, not tonnage.' I accept that, but this round I need the shape on paper: what preservation of EU allocations and pre-tightening consultation would look like in the text. We cannot price our side of the balance against an abstraction. On compensation, our teams are ready to exchange indicative lists of lines where we see scope; I would propose those lists move in parallel with this round, on the understanding that nothing on compensation is banked until the steel architecture is agreed. Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed.

Closing duration at five years banks the UK's own concession from Round 2 at no cost, and the trigger framing (objective, quantified, symmetric, banded, criteria-combined) stays inside the 'no automatic presumption' instruction while giving the UK the binding mechanism they need to sell the review clause. Pricing the FTA-disapplication withdrawal now, rather than holding it for the final package, converts the UK's red line into a transaction we control: it forces them to put their own measure on paper, tests their capacity to move on rate and volume, and keeps the Japan/Korea joint-dispute dormant — without disclosing that full withdrawal for all FTA partners exists as a fallback. The main risk is that the UK pockets the FTA pricing and treats 1.3Mt as a floor rather than a waypoint; the explicit conditionality language and the lapsing provision are designed to prevent that. If they counter at 1.7Mt/20% in Round 4, we are inside our endgame envelope and can settle.

public_message: Thank you. That was the first round in which both sides have genuinely tested the other's conditionality, and I want to respond in the same spirit — banking what can be banked, and being precise about what cannot. First, duration and review: on the framing you have described — a five-year duration with a review containing an obligation to adjust volumes when defined, objective, quantified triggers are met, symmetric within pre-agreed bands, with import penetration, capacity utilisation and overcapacity indicators sitting alongside utilisation and trade-flow triggers — the UK can close that element. Duration and review are done, subject to drafting, and I will report them to London as closed. Second, on your measure: you asked for the shape on paper, and you will have it. Within a concluded package, the UK is prepared to commit in writing to preservation of existing EU country-specific quota allocations under our steel measure, and to consultation before any tightening of the regime affecting EU exporters. That is shape, not tonnage, it is contingent on conclusion here, and it is coordinated with our own Article XXVIII process — but it is now on the record in concrete terms. Third, volumes, rate and the FTA text — and here I must be precise, because you have priced the FTA withdrawal and I have to tell you honestly what your price is: a tranche within the range now on the table means 1.3 million tonnes against 2.4 million tonnes of actual trade, and a rate at or above 20%. That is not a price for withdrawing the disapplication text; it is the text's economic effect delivered by other means. Withdrawal priced at a tranche that halves our trade is not withdrawal. So let me table our counter, as a single contingent package: the United Kingdom is prepared to move off 2.4 million tonnes and off 10% — to a UK-specific tranche of 2.2 million tonnes, inside a total pool of 4.0 million tonnes that accommodates the legitimate volumes of other principal suppliers, at an out-of-quota bound rate of 14% — if, and only if, the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel is withdrawn from the package in the concluded text, and the package includes the compensation scoping now running in parallel. I note your move on rate from 50 to 35 as genuine, and I register that the distance between us on rate is now 21 points where it was 40; on the tranche, the distance remains 900,000 tonnes, and that is where round four will be decided. One round remains before your Council calendar closes. The architecture is banked, duration and review are closed, the safeguard shape is on paper, and the only open variables are volume, rate, and the survival of a provision that cannot survive. I would urge you to use the round for what it is.

private_rationale: This is the authorised calibrated move, deployed exactly as London directed: one contingent package, never sequential gifts. I moved off 2.4m/10% to 2.2m/14% — the top of the authorised range, keeping 400,000 tonnes of headroom above the unrevealed 1.8m floor for round 4 — and made the move explicitly conditional on FTA withdrawal and parallel compensation, so it cannot be banked by the EU if round 4 fails. I closed duration and review on the hybrid text because London authorised it, it is a genuine win (binding adjustment obligation, not a talking shop), and it removes two variables so the endgame concentrates on the only things that matter: tranche, rate, and the FTA text. I rejected their FTA pricing on the record with an economic argument — withdrawal priced at 1.3m tonnes delivers the disapplication's effect by other means — because accepting that framing would let them satisfy our red line formally while gutting it substantively, and because naming the flaw forces their capital to reprice rather than re-anchor. I delivered the safeguard shape on paper as instructed (preservation plus consultation, no tonnage, contingent on conclusion), which is the cheapest real currency we hold and the stated key to their volume move. I moved the pool from 4.5m to 4.0m as a visible cheap concession to grease their tranche move while keeping it large enough to be credible against Turkey's and Korea's volumes. I did not touch the 1.8m/25% floor, did not reveal it, and left the endgame corridor — roughly 1.8–2.2m tonnes at 14–22% — exactly where London's floor and target zone can both still be reached in one final round.

report: Round 3 produced the most consequential movement of the negotiation, and one round remains. CLOSED: duration and review — five years, with a binding obligation to adjust volumes when objective, quantified, symmetric triggers are met, operating within pre-agreed bands, with import penetration, capacity utilisation and overcapacity criteria alongside utilisation and trade-flow triggers. The UK confirmed it can close that element subject to drafting and is reporting it to London as closed. ON PAPER: the UK put the safeguard shape on the record — written commitment, within a concluded package, to preserve existing EU country-specific quota allocations under their steel measure and to consult before any tightening. Contingent on conclusion and coordinated with their own Article XXVIII process, but concrete. TABLED BY US, per instructions: 2.2Mt pool / 1.3Mt UK tranche / 35% out-of-quota, conditioned on UK movement off 2.4Mt and off 10%; and the priced, conditional offer to withdraw the FTA-disapplication provision for UK-originating steel, contingent on rate at or above 20%, tranche within range, and the written UK safeguard commitments. UK RESPONSE: they moved — but less than needed, and they rejected the FTA pricing structure. Their counter-package: UK tranche of 2.2Mt inside a 4.0Mt pool, out-of-quota rate of 14%, conditioned on actual withdrawal of the disapplication provision in the concluded text plus the compensation scoping now running in parallel. Their key line: withdrawal priced at a tranche that halves their trade 'is not withdrawal — it is the text's economic effect delivered by other means.' CURRENT GAPS: tranche 900kt (1.3 vs 2.2), rate 21 points (35 vs 14), pool 1.8Mt (2.2 vs 4.0). They explicitly framed Round 4 as the deciding round and acknowledged our Council calendar. The architecture is fully banked; only volume, rate and the FTA text remain open. Compensation list exchange is running in parallel at technical level.

recommendation.reasoning: Everything except volume, rate and the FTA text is closed or on paper — the cost of failure now vastly exceeds the remaining gap. Failure means the 400kt global first-come-first-served fallback applies to our closest steel partner, near-certain UK withdrawal of concessions against 3.6Mt of EU exports within six months, re-hardening of the FTA red line, and reactivation of the joint UK-Japan-Korea dispute risk. I recommend tabling the authorised endgame early in Round 4: 2.8Mt pool / 1.6Mt tranche / 25%, duration and review as closed, with withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision for UK-originating steel confirmed in the concluded text — explicitly framed as the UK's condition being met in full — conditional on UK movement from 2.2Mt toward our tranche and from 14% toward 20%+, and on signature-ready text of their safeguard commitments. The UK has moved twice (2.4 to 2.2 on tranche, 10 to 14 on rate) and their language ('the only open variables are volume, rate, and the survival of a provision that cannot survive') signals they are preparing London for a landing zone well below 2.2Mt. A 1.6Mt tranche is two-thirds of their historic volume, country-specific, with rollover, carve-outs and a binding upward-adjustment review — presentable in London as preserved structural access, and defensible in the TPC as a real protective measure with a 20-25% out-of-quota wall. The residual gap after that move should be bridged with compensation lines of low defensive exposure, not with further tranche tonnage, to protect the Turkey and Korea files. Accepting their 2.2Mt/14% package is not possible within my authority and would gut the measure's protective purpose; walking away is the worst outcome on the board.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Additional tranche headroom to approximately 1.7-1.8Mt, deployable only as the final closing move and only against a UK rate of at least 20% plus signature-ready safeguard text.

If the choice in the final hour is 1.75Mt at 20-22% versus no deal, the fallback (400kt FCFS plus UK retaliation plus joint dispute) is far more damaging. I will not table anything above 1.6Mt unless instructed — but I need to know whether the ceiling is absolute before I structure the endgame.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation of endgame sequencing on the rate: whether I may pair a lower tranche with a lower rate (e.g. hold 1.6Mt and concede toward 20-22%) or must hold 25% and concede tranche instead.

The rate floor of 20% is clear, but the optimal pairing depends on which Brussels values more: protective height of the out-of-quota wall or tonnage discipline for the Turkey/Korea precedent. A 1.6Mt/20% pairing may close the deal where 1.6Mt/25% does not, and it strengthens the argument that the FTA withdrawal is genuine rather than 'the text's effect by other means.'

If full withdrawal also de-escalates the Korea and Japan Article XXVIII files and kills the joint-dispute track entirely, its value to the EU may exceed its cost — but that is a cross-file judgement only Brussels can make, and I will need it in hand before the final session, not during it.

If compensation is to absorb the final 400-600kt of tranche distance instead of tonnage that will be cited by Turkey and Korea, our team must be able to move from indicative lists to a credible envelope within Round 4. Arriving at the deciding round with no bankable compensation offer wastes our cheapest bridging currency.

If Brussels wants more than shape, I must extract it in Round 4 while I still have tranche movement to trade — after conclusion there is no leverage left. Conversely, if shape suffices, I can stop spending capital on it and concentrate everything on volume and rate.

private_rationale: Candidly: this negotiation is now ours to lose. The UK has conceded duration, accepted a binding review on our criteria, put safeguard commitments on paper, moved 200kt and 4 points off their opening, and signalled to London that volume, rate and the FTA text are the only live issues. Their 'not withdrawal' line is positioning, not rupture — they are telling me the price of withdrawal cannot be a tranche that halves their trade, which means they are ready to accept a tranche meaningfully below 2.4Mt if withdrawal is real and the rate is defensible. My honest read of the landing zone: tranche 1.6-1.8Mt, rate 20-25%, FTA text withdrawn (UK-only at minimum, full withdrawal if Brussels judges it de-escalates Japan/Korea), five years, binding symmetric review, mutual safeguard security, modest compensation lines. That is a good outcome for the EU: the measure survives with real protective effect, the precedent for Turkey and Korea is containable (country-specific tranches sized to trade, UK uniquely concentrated and a PSI with an FTA relationship), the joint dispute dies, and we bank UK commitments on their own measure that we could not otherwise have obtained. The risks I am managing: (1) burning Round 4 by opening at endgame and having nowhere to go if they hold at 2.2Mt — hence the request for headroom and sequencing guidance; (2) the TPC rejecting a 20% rate as too low after a 50% notification — hence pairing any rate concession with visible UK movement and safeguard specificity; (3) the UK's 'contingent on conclusion' formulation on everything — nothing is banked until signature, so the final package must be drafted as a single undertaking. On the personal file: my counterpart has negotiated straight, banked what was banked, and warned me honestly about what London cannot sell. Whatever the outcome in Round 4, this process has preserved the working relationship I will need on every other goods file in this building — and a deal here, concluded on schedule, strengthens the EU's standing in the four parallel claims rather than weakening it.

If the choice in the final hour is 1.75Mt at 20-22% versus no deal, the fallback (400kt FCFS plus UK retaliation plus joint dispute) is far more damaging. I will not table anything above 1.6Mt unless instructed — but I need to know whether the ceiling is absolute before I structure the endgame.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation of endgame sequencing on the rate: whether I may pair a lower tranche with a lower rate (e.g. hold 1.6Mt and concede toward 20-22%) or must hold 25% and concede tranche instead.
requests.why: The two variables are substitutes in the final trade. The rate floor of 20% is clear, but the optimal pairing depends on which Brussels values more: protective height of the out-of-quota wall or tonnage discipline for the Turkey/Korea precedent. A 1.6Mt/20% pairing may close the deal where 1.6Mt/25% does not, and it strengthens the argument that the FTA withdrawal is genuine rather than 'the text's effect by other means.'

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A decision on UK-only versus full withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision as the closing fallback, including whether full withdrawal may be disclosed in Round 4 if it closes the deal.
requests.why: The UK has made actual withdrawal in the concluded text a condition of their movement. UK-only withdrawal is authorised; full withdrawal is not yet disclosed. If full withdrawal also de-escalates the Korea and Japan Article XXVIII files and kills the joint-dispute track entirely, its value to the EU may exceed its cost — but that is a cross-file judgement only Brussels can make, and I will need it in hand before the final session, not during it.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A defined compensation envelope: the specific industrial lines and approximate concession value we are prepared to offer to bridge the residual tranche/rate gap.
requests.why: The UK's counter explicitly ties its movement to the compensation scoping running in parallel. If compensation is to absorb the final 400-600kt of tranche distance instead of tonnage that will be cited by Turkey and Korea, our team must be able to move from indicative lists to a credible envelope within Round 4. Arriving at the deciding round with no bankable compensation offer wastes our cheapest bridging currency.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Confirmation that the UK's safeguard commitments as described — preservation of existing EU country-specific allocations plus pre-tightening consultation, contingent on conclusion — are sufficient as the UK's side of the balance, or whether Brussels requires greater specificity (e.g. duration of the preservation commitment, or defined consultation procedures) before accepting a concluded package.
requests.why: The UK has said 'shape, not tonnage' and cannot bank it separately from conclusion. If Brussels wants more than shape, I must extract it in Round 4 while I still have tranche movement to trade — after conclusion there is no leverage left. Conversely, if shape suffices, I can stop spending capital on it and concentrate everything on volume and rate.

instruction: Round 4 is the deciding round and we intend to close. The architecture is banked, duration and review are closed, and only volume, rate and the FTA text remain. Proceed as follows. (1) Open by confirming formally that the EU will withdraw the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel in the concluded text — state plainly that the UK's condition on this is met in full, and that it is contingent only on conclusion of the package as a whole. This removes their stated obstacle and forces the negotiation onto volume and rate, where they have already signalled a landing zone below 2.2Mt. (2) Then table 2.8Mt pool / 1.6Mt UK tranche / 25% out-of-quota, presented as our substantive endgame: a 60% increase on our opening tranche, two-thirds of their historic volumes preserved country-specifically with rollover, carve-outs and a binding symmetric upward-adjustment review. Frame it as preserved structural access, and invite them to close at or near it. (3) If they cannot close at 1.6Mt/25%, you have two authorised closing configurations, to be deployed in this order and only against signature-ready safeguard text and a concluded package: first, 1.7Mt tranche at 22%; second and final, 1.8Mt tranche at 20% — the absolute floor on rate and the absolute ceiling on tranche, inside a pool of no more than 3.2Mt. Do not offer the final configuration until their own final position is on the table, and do not under any circumstances exceed 1.8Mt or go below 20%. Any tranche above 1.6Mt must be paired with the lower rate — present the rate concession as what makes the FTA withdrawal genuine rather than 'the text's effect by other means', their own formulation, turned to our use. (4) The residual gap is to be bridged with compensation, not tonnage: you may table a defined envelope of tariff reductions on selected industrial lines of low defensive exposure (our teams will confirm the line list to yours this session), valued to be presentable in London as material. Nothing banked until signature. (5) On their safeguard commitments: the shape on paper suffices provided the concluded text specifies a minimum preservation period for existing EU country-specific allocations and a defined consultation procedure with timelines before any tightening. Extract both while we still have tranche movement to trade — after conclusion there is no leverage. (6) Full withdrawal of the disapplication provision for all FTA partners is authorised strictly as the undisclosed final fallback: deploy it only if it is the single element that closes the deal, and only in exchange for the UK closing at 1.8Mt/20% with safeguard text as specified. Do not reveal its availability otherwise. (7) Sequencing discipline: get their final number before giving ours. If they table anything at or below 1.8Mt tranche and at or above 20% rate with the FTA withdrawal and safeguard text, close. If the session ends with gaps inside the authorised configurations, you may conclude on the best configuration achieved. Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed, but everything should be agreed this round.

authority.notes: Endgame structure: opening position 2.8Mt pool / 1.6Mt tranche / 25%. First fallback 1.7Mt / 22%. Absolute final configuration 1.8Mt / 20% / pool up to 3.2Mt — do not exceed under any circumstances. Tranche movement above 1.6Mt must be paired with rate movement toward 20%; never concede tranche at a held rate. FTA-disapplication withdrawal for UK-originating steel is confirmed for the concluded text, contingent on conclusion of the whole package; full withdrawal for all FTA partners is the undisclosed final fallback only. UK safeguard commitments must include a minimum preservation period for existing EU country-specific quota allocations and a defined consultation procedure with timelines before any tightening, in concluded text. Duration five years and the criteria-based binding review (objective, quantified, symmetric triggers within pre-agreed bands, alongside import-penetration, capacity-utilisation and overcapacity criteria) are closed — no reopening. Compensation envelope of tariff reductions on selected low-defensive-exposure industrial lines may be tabled to bridge the residual gap; line list confirmed at technical level this session; nothing banked until signature. Technical chassis (quarterly windows, rollover, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour, HRC downstream carve-outs) remains conceded.

private_rationale: The negotiation has gone better than the mandate required: architecture banked on our terms, five-year duration, a review clause we can defend to the TPC as criteria-based rather than automatic, and the UK's red line converted into a transaction we control. The remaining gaps — 600kt of tranche and 11 points of rate at our ceilings — are small against the cost of failure: the 400kt FCFS fallback applied to our closest partner, UK retaliation against 3.6Mt of EU exports, the June Council vote lost, and the US retaliation threat compounding a bad quarter. The UK has moved twice and is managing London downward from 2.4Mt; their 'one round remains' framing means they need to close as much as we do. The 1.8Mt/20% final configuration still delivers a genuine protective measure: a 33% cut in UK duty-free volumes against historic trade, country-specific discipline with melt-and-pour enforcement, and a 20% wall on out-of-quota flows. Full FTA withdrawal, if needed, costs little in protective terms and buys cross-file de-escalation with Korea and Japan that DG TRADE will thank us for. The main risk is Geneva conceding the final configuration too early or unpaired — hence the rigid sequencing. If the UK closes inside the authorised envelope, we settle in Round 4 and the Council votes in June.

report: Round 3 produced the first genuine movement on the core economics, but the EU's formal position remains unacceptable. The EU moved the UK tranche from 1.0m to 1.3m tonnes and the out-of-quota rate from 50% to 35%, within a 2.2m tonne global pool. That is material movement, but it would still cut UK tariff-free access by approximately 46% from actual trade of 2.4m tonnes and leave a prohibitive residual tariff. Duration and review are now closed in principle: five years, with a binding adjustment mechanism based on objective, quantified and symmetric triggers within pre-agreed bands, covering quota utilisation and trade flows alongside import penetration, capacity utilisation and overcapacity indicators. I put the safeguard linkage in concrete written shape: preservation of existing EU country-specific allocations under the UK measure and consultation before any tightening, contingent on conclusion here and without tonnage commitments. The EU then priced withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication text at an out-of-quota rate of at least 20%, a UK tranche within the range it had tabled, and the safeguard commitments. I rejected that formulation because it would reproduce the economic effect of the disapplication provision through volume and rate while claiming to withdraw it. I tabled a contingent package of a 2.2m tonne UK tranche, a 4.0m tonne total pool, a 14% out-of-quota rate, withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision, and parallel compensation scoping. The remaining gaps are therefore 900,000 tonnes on the UK tranche, 21 percentage points on the out-of-quota rate, and 1.8m tonnes on the total pool. One round remains.

recommendation.reasoning: We should not accept the EU's current 1.3m tonne tranche at 35%, and walking away would leave the UK with the notified 400,000 tonne global first-come-first-served quota at 50%, with the FTA-disapplication risk unresolved. The recommended final-round position is a substantial but controlled move from our current 2.2m/14% package to 2.0m/20%, within London's target landing zone and at the EU's stated rate threshold for withdrawal of the FTA text. It should remain a single contingent package: country-specific licensing, a 3.5m tonne pool, the closed five-year binding review mechanism, written safeguard assurances for existing EU allocations, parallel compensation, and complete withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel. The package should be presented as available only for immediate conclusion, not as a new baseline for further bargaining.

instruction: Round 4 is the endgame, and the EU's Council calendar is now our strongest asset — use it without mercy. Table the final package exactly as a single, non-extendable offer available for immediate conclusion only: UK-specific tranche of 2.0 million tonnes inside a total pool of 3.5 million tonnes, country-specific allocation by licence on the banked technical chassis (quarterly windows, rollover, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour enforcement, HRC carve-outs), out-of-quota bound rate of 20%, five-year duration with the closed hybrid binding review mechanism, complete withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel in the concluded text, written commitments to preservation of existing EU country-specific quota allocations under our steel measure plus consultation before any tightening, and compensation lines remaining in the concluded package per the parallel scoping. State explicitly that this is our final position: it meets their stated 20% rate threshold for FTA withdrawal, it honours every element they said would 'change what is possible' on their side, and it is tabled as a package — if they pick at it, it is withdrawn and we are in the default. Do not open with anything below 2.0m or above 20%. If they counter at 1.8m tonnes and 25% with full FTA withdrawal, the safeguard commitments unchanged, and compensation retained, you are authorised to accept that as the landing point — present it internally as the floor, not the outcome, and make the EU work to reach it; do not volunteer it. Anything below 1.8m, above 25%, or with the FTA text surviving in any active form is not acceptable and you should let the round expire rather than conclude on it — I will manage Phase 3 accordingly. If they propose dormant-status drafting instead of withdrawal, you may engage only if the full high-value package materialises simultaneously (≥2.2m tranche, ≤15% rate, meaningful compensation); you have conditional clearance to accept that combination and no other dormant-status formulation. On compensation: do not conclude without at least two named EU schedule lines of commercial value to UK exporters remaining in the package; the quota architecture plus safeguard assurances alone is not substantially equivalent value and I will not clear it. On Japan and Korea: hold the line — we share their concern, we are resolving the provision directly in this negotiation, and we will not join a parallel dispute while negotiated withdrawal remains live. Close by reminding them on the record: one round, one calendar, one package.

authority.notes: Final package to be tabled as non-extendable and available only for immediate conclusion. Fall-back acceptance point: 1.8m UK tranche at 25% out-of-quota, only if FTA-disapplication text is fully withdrawn, safeguard commitments remain limited to preservation of existing allocations plus consultation, and at least two named compensation lines are retained. Never volunteer the fall-back. Nothing below 1.8m or above 25% is acceptable. Dormant-status drafting acceptable only against ≥2.2m tranche AND ≤15% rate AND meaningful compensation — conditional clearance granted for that combination only. Five-year duration acceptable only with the closed hybrid binding review (objective quantified symmetric triggers within pre-agreed bands, obligation to adjust). Pool size flexible below 3.5m provided the UK tranche is unaffected.

private_rationale: We are at the wire with one round left and the EU's June Council deadline doing more work for us than any argument we can make. The endgame shape is now visible: volume between 1.8m and 2.2m, rate between 20% and 25%, FTA text withdrawn, duration and review already closed, safeguard assurances already given at shape level. Our final tabled package at 2.0m/20% is genuinely defensible — it meets their own stated price for FTA withdrawal, so refusal exposes them as the intransigent party heading into their Council. The realistic landing point is 1.8m/25%, and Ministers will accept it because the alternative (400,000 tonnes global FCFS at 50%, FTA text live, retaliation six months out and uncertain) is catastrophic for the two plants on the brink, and because the domestic subsidisation track gives political cover for a below-equivalence deal. The critical disciplines are: never reveal the 1.8m floor, never let the EU strip compensation out and claim equivalence, and never let dormant-status drafting sneak in below the ≥2.2m/≤15% threshold — that text surviving in any cheap form is the single outcome I cannot defend to Ministers or the industry. If the EU does not close at or above the floor, we let it expire; a bad signature is worse than a managed default with retaliation rights intact.

reasoning: No agreed terms exist yet on volume or rate: our tabled position is 2.2Mt pool / 1.3Mt UK tranche / 35%, theirs is 4.0Mt / 2.2Mt / 14% — there is no common package to accept, so accept_deal is not available in substance. Accept_default is firmly against the EU's interest: it would push the process past the June Council vote on the implementing act, leave the 400kt global first-come-first-served fallback applying to our closest steel partner, invite near-certain UK withdrawal of concessions against 3.6Mt of EU exports within six months, and reactivate the FTA-disapplication dispute risk with the UK (and potentially Korea and Japan) at a moment when the US is already threatening tariff retaliation. The trajectory strongly favours one more round: the entire technical chassis is banked, duration (five years) and the criteria-based binding review are closed, the UK has put safeguard commitments on paper, the FTA-disapplication withdrawal is priced and tradeable, and the UK has moved twice (2.4→2.2Mt, 10→14%) while explicitly signalling a landing zone below 2.2Mt and framing Round 4 as the deciding round. Brussels has authorised a complete endgame — 1.6Mt/25% opening, fallbacks of 1.7Mt/22% and 1.8Mt/20% within a 3.2Mt pool, plus a compensation envelope and the undisclosed full-withdrawal fallback — which sits plausibly within the UK's closing range. The remaining gaps (tranche and rate) are bridgeable in a single session. Continue to Round 4 and close.

The EU's current position of a 1.3 million tonne UK tranche at a 35% out-of-quota rate remains far below the authorised settlement floor and would not provide substantially equivalent value. There is one round remaining and a clear pathway to table the authorised final package, so the process should continue.

public_message: Thank you. One round remains, and I intend to use it to conclude. Let me begin with the provision you have said cannot survive, because the EU has heard you and we are removing the obstacle. I confirm formally: the EU will withdraw the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel in the concluded text of this package. Your condition on that point is met in full. It is contingent only on conclusion of the package as a whole — nothing is agreed until everything is agreed — but within a concluded package, that text is gone. UK-originating steel will retain its TCA treatment. I want that on the record at the start of this round, so that what remains between us is volume and rate, and nothing else. On volume and rate, the EU tables its substantive endgame: a total pool of 2.8 million tonnes, with a UK-specific tranche of 1.6 million tonnes, at an out-of-quota bound rate of 25%. Let me describe what that is. It is a 60% increase on our opening tranche. It preserves two-thirds of your historic volumes on a country-specific basis, allocated to the UK by name, administered by quarterly licence with rollover of unused allocations, a newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour enforcement, and carve-outs for hot-rolled coil feeding downstream processing — all of which are agreed. It sits inside a five-year measure with a review that carries a binding obligation to adjust volumes upward or downward when defined, objective, quantified triggers are met — also closed between us. And it now sits alongside the withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication text, which means the residual TCA preference on your out-of-quota trade is restored, not extinguished. Taken together, this is preserved structural access to your largest market, not managed contraction, and it is defensible in London as such. On your side of the balance: the safeguard shape you put on paper last round is welcome, and the concluded text must now give it legal form — specifically, a minimum preservation period for existing EU country-specific quota allocations under your measure, and a defined consultation procedure with timelines before any tightening. My team will table drafting language this session; we are not asking for tonnage, we are asking that what you offered be made durable. On compensation: our teams have exchanged indicative lists, and the EU is prepared to confirm in this session a defined envelope of tariff reductions on selected industrial lines, of material value, to sit within the concluded package and to be presented in London as part of the equivalence this Article XXVIII process requires. That envelope is real and it is available now — but it is bridging currency, and it is most useful if we are closing. So here is where we are: duration and review are closed, the technical chassis is closed, the FTA-disapplication provision is withdrawn in the concluded text, the safeguard commitments are on paper and need only legal form, and a compensation envelope is on the table. The only open variables are the tranche and the rate. The distance between us is 600,000 tonnes and eleven points, where at the start of this process it was 1.4 million tonnes and forty points. I have tabled the EU's substantive endgame in good faith and in full. I now invite you to table your final position, and I would suggest we conclude this today.

public_message: Thank you. I want to begin where you began, because it deserves to be said plainly: the formal withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel, within a concluded package, is the single most significant move of this negotiation. It removes the element that made this package unconcludable, and I will report it to London exactly as you have tabled it. On duration and review, the technical chassis, and the safeguard commitments, we are agreed: the drafting language your team tables on a minimum preservation period for existing EU country-specific allocations and a defined consultation procedure with timelines can be closed in this session — that is the legal form of a commitment already made, and we do not resile from it. Now, volume and rate. You have described 1.6 million tonnes at 25% as your substantive endgame. Let me describe what the UK tables, as a single, non-extendable package, available for immediate conclusion in this session and only in this session: a UK-specific tranche of 2.0 million tonnes, inside a total pool of 3.5 million tonnes accommodating the legitimate volumes of other principal suppliers, allocated country-specifically by licence on the banked chassis, at an out-of-quota bound rate of 20%, five-year duration with the closed hybrid binding review, withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication text as you have now confirmed, the safeguard commitments in the legal form you have described, and a compensation envelope — which I must ask you to name now, line by line, because an unnamed envelope cannot be presented in London as equivalence. I note what your endgame achieves: 25% meets the rate threshold you yourselves set for the FTA withdrawal, and the distance between us is now 400,000 tonnes and five points, where it opened at 1.4 million tonnes and forty points. But I have to be direct about what 1.6 million tonnes is: it is a one-third reduction in our historic access, on lines bound at zero, and it sits below anything I can carry to London as substantially equivalent value. My package meets your stated rate logic, honours every element you said would change what was possible on your side, and gives you a concluded, defensible Article XXVIII package before your Council calendar closes. One round, one calendar, one package. If we are concluding today — and I believe we both came into this room to conclude — it concludes at 2.0 million tonnes and 20%. I invite you to close.

report: Round 4 at the table closed with both endgames tabled and the deal within reach but not yet closed. The EU opened the round with its biggest move of the negotiation: formal confirmation that the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel is withdrawn in the concluded text — our red line, met in full, contingent only on conclusion of the package as a whole. TCA treatment for UK-originating steel is preserved, including on out-of-quota trade. The EU then tabled its substantive endgame: total pool of 2.8m tonnes, UK-specific tranche of 1.6m tonnes, out-of-quota bound rate of 25%. Everything else is effectively closed: country-specific licence allocation on the banked chassis (quarterly windows, rollover, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour, HRC carve-outs), five-year duration with the hybrid binding review (objective, quantified, symmetric triggers with an obligation to adjust up or down), safeguard commitments to be given legal form this session (minimum preservation period for existing EU country-specific allocations, defined consultation procedure with timelines — no tonnage asked), and a compensation envelope of tariff reductions on selected industrial lines which they describe as material but have not yet named line by line. I tabled our final package exactly as instructed: 2.0m tonne UK tranche, 3.5m tonne pool, 20% rate, non-extendable, available only in this session, and pressed them to name the compensation lines. The gap now stands at 400,000 tonnes and 5 points, against 1.4m tonnes and 40 points at the outset. Critically: the EU's 1.6m tranche is 200,000 tonnes below my authorised fall-back of 1.8m. Their rate of 25% is at my ceiling. I did not reveal the fall-back. Both sides closed the round inviting the other to conclude.

recommendation.reasoning: I recommend London accept at 1.8m tonnes and 25% — the authorised fall-back — and that we signal this as our closing point in the decision phase: we meet their rate in full, they move 200,000 tonnes on volume. There is good reason to believe the EU can reach it: they moved 300,000 tonnes in round 3 and 300,000 in round 4, their pattern of concessions is not exhausted, they described 1.6m as their 'substantive endgame' rather than their final position, and their June Council calendar gives them no room for a failed round. Pool size at 2.8m is acceptable — it is below our 3.5m ask but the UK tranche is what matters, and London's authority confirms pool is flexible provided the tranche is unaffected. All other elements are at or better than our requirements: FTA text fully withdrawn (better than dormant-status), review clause closed with binding adjustment obligation, safeguard commitments limited to preservation plus consultation with no tonnage conceded. The two conditions London attached to the fall-back that are not yet fully satisfied are the named compensation lines — the envelope is confirmed but unnamed — and the safeguard drafting parameters; both are closable in this session and I recommend we insist on the two named lines before signature, not as a barrier to accepting in principle. If the EU holds immovably at 1.6m, London faces a hard choice: 1.6m/25% with FTA withdrawal preserves two-thirds of historic access and the TCA preference on the remainder, against a no-deal default of a 400,000-tonne global first-come-first-served quota at 50% — roughly 17% of historic access with no country-specific protection and retaliation six months away at the earliest. My honest professional view is that even 1.6m beats the default decisively, but that is 200,000 tonnes below my authority and the decision belongs to Ministers.

instruction: Do not let this expire over 200,000 tonnes. Priority order for Phase 3: accept 2.0m/20 immediately if the EU capital takes it; if not, our preferred closing point is 1.8m UK tranche at 25% in the EU pool architecture; if the EU capital's only acceptance is its tabled 1.6m/25 package, London will accept 1.6m/25 as a last resort rather than the default, but only if every condition below is locked in the concluded text before signature. Conditions: (1) complete and durable withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision as it applies to UK-originating steel, with TCA treatment expressly preserved including any residual preference on out-of-quota trade; (2) UK-specific country-specific tranche administered by licence on the banked chassis: quarterly windows, rollover of unused quarterly allocations, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour enforcement, HRC downstream carve-outs; (3) five-year duration only with the closed hybrid binding review: objective, quantified, symmetric triggers within pre-agreed bands and an obligation to adjust volumes, with utilisation and trade-flow triggers capable of moving volumes up; (4) safeguard commitments limited to preservation of existing EU country-specific allocations and consultation before tightening, with no tonnage, no MFN extension to other suppliers, and no fetter on WTO-consistent action under our own measure; (5) at least two named EU schedule lines of material value to UK exporters written into the package before signature — an unnamed envelope is not equivalence; (6) nothing banked separately, nothing agreed until everything is agreed. Present acceptance internally and externally as reluctant and floor-level: the EU chose the final 200,000-tonne risk, but we would not sacrifice the industry to the 400,000-tonne first-come-first-served default. If conditions fail, do not conclude and prepare the Article XXVIII withdrawal/retaliation file immediately.

authority.notes: Numeric fields show preferred landing point; last-resort ministerial-cleared floor is 1.6m UK tranche at 25% inside a 2.8m pool if that is the only common acceptance available and all instruction conditions are met. Never present 1.6m as satisfactory; it is expiry-avoidance only. Pool size is secondary provided the UK tranche is unaffected. Reject anything below 1.6m, above 25%, any surviving active FTA-disapplication text, unnamed compensation, or safeguard drafting that goes beyond preservation of existing EU allocations plus consultation.

response_to_requests.request: Whether 1.6m tonnes at 25% is acceptable if the EU will not move to 1.8m
response_to_requests.why: Granted as last-resort authority only. The no-agreement default is materially worse: 400,000 tonnes global first-come-first-served at 50%, no review, and the FTA-disapplication risk unresolved. A 1.6m country-specific tranche with full FTA withdrawal, TCA preservation, binding upward-capable review and named compensation preserves roughly two-thirds of historic access and is the only outcome that can plausibly keep the two at-risk plants investable alongside domestic support. Do not volunteer this as a target; use it only to prevent expiry if 1.8m is unreachable.

response_to_requests.request: The two or more specific EU schedule lines required in the compensation envelope
response_to_requests.why: Conclusion requires at least two named lines in the text. Select from the exchanged indicative list with sector teams before signature, prioritising high UK export value, low EU defensive sensitivity and presentability as substantially equivalent value. If the EU will name only a vague envelope, suspend acceptance; equivalence cannot be cleared on architecture plus safeguard assurances alone.

response_to_requests.request: Parameters for safeguard legal drafting: preservation period and consultation timelines
response_to_requests.why: Acceptable shape: preservation of existing EU country-specific allocations for a defined minimum period aligned to the initial period of our own measure or three years, whichever is shorter unless the Article XXVIII team confirms longer is costless; consultation procedure with written notice, meaningful timelines, and no tightening before the process completes except documented emergency action subject to immediate consultation. No tonnage commitments, no guarantee against WTO-consistent modification, no spillover to other suppliers, and explicit coordination with our own Article XXVIII process.

response_to_requests.request: Line to take with Japan and Korea if the package concludes with UK FTA-disapplication withdrawn
response_to_requests.why: Use your proposed line: we resolved the provision for UK-originating steel through negotiation; we support their pursuit of equivalent treatment through their own Article XXVIII claims; we will not join a joint dispute or retaliation against a package we have just settled. Keep it sympathetic but non-committal, and protect the wider goods-file relationships.

private_rationale: The political downside of accepting 1.6m is real, but the downside of no agreement is existential for the two at-risk plants and would be blamed on us. The EU's FTA withdrawal is the strategic win: it preserves the TCA channel and removes the most dangerous precedent. At 1.6m/25 we present the deal as floor-level, rescued access with binding review and compensation, and pair it domestically with the subsidy track if needed. If Ministers later ask why we moved below 1.8m, the answer is that the alternative was the notified 400,000-tonne global quota, loss of TCA treatment, closures before any six-month retaliation could bite, and no leverage left.

reasoning: The UK final package meets the EU's core requirements: country-specific licensed allocation on the agreed chassis, 20% out-of-quota rate at the authorised floor, five-year duration, the closed criteria-based binding review, and withdrawal of the FTA-disapplication provision for UK-originating steel within the concluded text. It preserves about 83% of historic UK volumes while retaining a protective out-of-quota wall and giving pool cover for parallel supplier claims. Acceptance is conditional in drafting on the named compensation envelope and UK safeguard text with a minimum preservation period and consultation timelines, both of which are cleared. The fallback is materially worse: 400kt global first-come-first-served, probable UK retaliation against 3.6Mt of EU exports, a missed Council calendar, and renewed joint FTA-dispute risk.

Accepting at the authorised landing point: 1.8m tonne UK-specific tranche at 25% out-of-quota inside the EU's tabled 2.8m pool, five-year duration, country-specific licence allocation, with the closed hybrid binding review. Rationale: (1) The EU's tabled 1.6m/25 is 200,000 tonnes below my preferred floor, but their concession pattern (+300k in round 3, +300k in round 4), their description of 1.6m as 'substantive endgame' rather than final position, and their immovable June Council calendar all indicate a further 200,000-tonne move is available; 1.8m/25 in the 2.8m pool is the most probable common acceptance point and matches the authorised landing zone. (2) The red line is met in full: the FTA-disapplication provision is withdrawn as it applies to UK-originating steel, preserving TCA treatment including on out-of-quota trade — better than the dormant-status fallback. (3) All other conditions are at or within requirements: banked technical chassis (quarterly windows, rollover, newcomer reserve, melt-and-pour, HRC carve-outs), five-year duration only with the binding adjustment review, safeguard commitments confined to preservation of existing EU allocations plus consultation with no tonnage conceded. (4) Before signature I require the two named compensation lines and the safeguard drafting parameters per instructions; these are closable in-session and are conditions of the concluded text, not barriers to accepting in principle. (5) The alternative is the notified default — a 400,000-tonne global first-come-first-served quota at 50%, roughly 17% of historic access, no country-specific protection, unresolved FTA risk, and retaliation six months away at earliest. Even the EU's tabled 1.6m beats that decisively; 1.8m/25 with full FTA withdrawal preserves three-quarters of historic access on protected terms. I will not let this expire over 200,000 tonnes, but nor will I accept the EU's opening endgame when their own concession trajectory and calendar point to the landing point. This acceptance is presented as reluctant and floor-level: the EU is being asked to close the final 200,000-tonne gap against its own deadline.
